title: Staff Stitchboard — Weekly catchup (2026-10-14)
content:
Attendees: Elena Park (chair), Marcus Liu, Priya Desai, Owen Gallagher, Sara Kim, Tomás Rivas (ops), Li Wei (sre - remote), notes captured live.

Objective: Lightweight cross-team sync to stitch platform, serving runtime, and private-deployments priorities into next sprint. Focus on 1) incident follow-ups, 2) capacity & scaling forecast for Dedicated, 3) rollout gating for new batching kernel.

Top-line summary / TL;DR:
- Incident INF-2345 (KV cache regression) root cause identified; mitigation in canary, rollback planned if metrics don't improve by 10/16 EOD.
- Dedicated forecast calls for +2 GPU pools by mid-Nov for enterprise onboarding (queue: enterprise-onboard-qa). Need procurement + infra quotas confirmed.
- Batching kernel (v3) shows 12–18% cost savings in perf bench but regresses tail latency on >2048 tokens. Decision: enable canary on low-latency routes only.

Discussion notes (rough):
- Incident recap (Priya): KV cache change in runtime v2.11 caused cache invalidation when token prefix contained unicode combining chars. Repro steps attached in INF-2345. Symptoms: increased p99 from 230ms -> 450ms for small-chat workload at 20 RPS.
  - Short term: deployed kinetic-cache-fix patch to canary group (10% traffic).
  - SRE asks for break-glass plan: rollback helm chart + traffic shift script (Tomás).
  - Decision: keep canary running 48h, measure p50/p95/p99 and error rates; if p99 > 350ms revert.

- Batching kernel rollout (Owen): kernel v3 increases async batching efficiency; internal bench shows 15% token/sec improvement on A100 for seq len 512. But on long sequences (>2048) there is a jitter in op scheduling causing tail outliers.
  - Action: create short experiment in staging with synthetic >2048 token traces (Elena -> assign to Owen). Use real traffic sampling to validate.
  - Canary plan: route low-latency labeled routes (search, chat-ux-lite) to kernel v3; keep high-LAT routes on v2. Failover policy: immediate fallback to v2 on >2% tail violation.

- Dedicated capacity forecast (Marcus): two inbound enterprise customers with committed go-live windows (Nov 20 and Dec 5). Current dedicated pool slots at 14/16 (logical). To meet SLA burst, need to provision two additional pools and reserve GPU quota. Procurement/CloudOps ask: submit quota ticket by 10/18.
  - Action: Marcus to file quota request + cost estimate (due 10/16). Platform-eng to prepare terraform module update for pool provisioning (Owen).

- Private (VPC) onboarding checklist (Sara): compliance artifacts mostly ready; outstanding: KMS rotation policy and audit export for one customer. Compliance owner flagged need for key-handover runbook.
  - Action: Sara + Li Wei to draft runbook and mock key-rotation test (due 10/22).

Metrics snapshot (as reported in Console at 09:30 PDT):
- Global p50: 72ms (stable), p95: 210ms (up 8%), p99: 410ms (up 75% from baseline) — correlated with INF-2345.
- Serving throughput: 4.7M tokens/min (steady).
- Dedicated utilization: 87% avg, short bursts to 98% during EMEA morning window.

Risks / blocking items:
- Quota approval lag could push Dedicated provisioning beyond Nov commitments. Mitigation: propose temporary overcommit on existing pools; evaluate scheduled burst windows with customers.
- Kernel v3 tail-risk remains unknown for long sequences; must not expose default traffic until verified.
- Incidents backlog: three separate cache-related tickets in triage — need dedicated cycle to reduce mean time to fix.

Decisions made:
- Keep KV-cache canary live 48h; rollback threshold set (p99 > 350ms or error rate +1%). Owner: Priya.
- Restrict kernel v3 canary to labeled low-latency routes. Owner: Owen.
- File quota request for +2 GPU pools by 10/18. Owner: Marcus.
- Draft KMS rotation runbook for Private by 10/22. Owners: Sara, Li Wei.

Action items (concrete):
1) Priya: collect canary telemetry dashboard (p50/p95/p99, errors) and post to INF-2345; check-in 10/16 morning.
2) Owen: synthetic >2048 token experiment in staging; share results in #eng-platform by 10/19.
3) Marcus: submit cloud quota ticket + cost breakdown for +2 pools; attach expected customer commit docs; due 10/16.
4) Sara & Li Wei: KMS rotation runbook + mock test plan; schedule dry-run with compliance; due 10/22.
5) Elena: produce short note for Exec on impact & mitigation plan if Dedicated provisioning delays (deliverable 10/17).
6) Tomás: prepare rollback script for helm traffic-shift and runbook for break-glass; due 10/15 EOD.

Parking lot / follow-ups:
- Long-term: revisit KV cache encoding handling across languages (python/java/node edge cases). Consider adding unit tests for unicode combining sequences. (R&D, product infra)
- Investigate burst autosizing policy for EMEA morning window (SRE + infra).
- Evaluate model-quantization policy impact on tail latency when combined with kernel v3.

Notes to self / informal lines (captured verbatim from conversation):
- "We shipped a cache tweak last sprint that helped CPU but tripped over emoji sequences" — Priya, laughing but serious.
- "If we rely on sampling only, we miss the 1% traffic that trips the tail — need targeted synthetic" — Li Wei.
- TODO: add an ops-channel alert runbook link to the canary dashboards.

Next meeting: same cadence, Wednesday 2026-10-21 09:00 PT. Proposed focus: post-canary readouts, Dedicated provisioning status, and a short deep-dive on autoscaling heuristics.

Attachments / references (internal):
- INF-2345 incident page: see linked_artifacts.
- Perf bench notes (serving-runtime PR 789) — bench raw logs attached in PR.
- Dedicated onboarding tracker (sheet): https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1QDedicatedForecastExample

End of notes.

-- Elena
